name: Slicked-back bun

lead:
A slicked-back bun smooths the hair flat against the head, often from a center part, and gathers it into a bun at the back or crown. Pulling the hair away from the face exposes the forehead, brow and jaw, so the style is used to emphasise facial structure.
Buns are made by pulling hair back and twisting, braiding or coiling it, then securing it with ties or pins.

paras: Hair is combed back, typically with a styling product for the sleek finish, then gathered and secured. Bun placement affects the effect: a high bun is described as youthful, a messy bun as relaxed.
No health risks are specific to the style.

angle.text: The style clears hair from the face, putting emphasis on facial features, and gives a deliberate, groomed look.

lead: A slicked-back bun is a sleek bun hairstyle in which hair is smoothed back, often from a center part, and gathered into a bun. It is a variant of the broader bun family, which men and women have worn in many cultures.[1]

Topknot-style buns are historical: ancient Chinese men wore a topknot, Japanese men the chonmage and Joseon-era Korean men the sangtu. The modern man bun likely began around 2010 in London, with search interest rising steeply from 2013 to 2015.[1]
For looks, pulling hair back exposes the face. Bun placement carries social connotations: a high bun is described as youthful and provocative, a messy bun as relaxed.[1]

paras: Buns are formed by pulling hair back and twisting, braiding or coiling it, then securing it with ties, pins, sticks or a donut-shaped insert.[1]

Topknots appear across many cultures; Romans associated them with groups such as the Goths and Vandals, and the Qing government required the Manchu queue.[1] The modern man bun trend likely began in London around 2010.[1]

Search interest in the man bun rises steeply.[1]
